newsitem.title: USA: Escambia County, Fla., rejects environmental tax.
newsitem.headline: Escambia County, Fla., rejects environmental tax.

text.p: Voters in Florida's Escambia County narrowly rejected a property tax increase to save environmentally sensitive land, elections officials said Friday.

The measure was defeated 51 percent to 49 percent, a difference of 1,943 votes. It would have increased property taxes by 25 cents per $1,000 of assessed value for five years, raising $6.5 million to help buy 7,000 acres of the Perdido Pitcher Plant Prarie.

The land west of Pensacola is home to the rare carnivorous pitcher plant, which eats mosquitos and other insects. Supporters of the proposal said they would try to persuade the state to purchase the land for preservation.
